rationale: Acceptance did not run (no extractable spec criteria), which caps confidence at low; the standards audit found 8/17 commit subjects violating the conventional-commit format (blocking). 11 findings kept: doctor-parse.js/doctor-groups.js parsing fragility (unrecognized-icon drop, six-space hint match, AWS-CLI single-item assumption, agent-name split, info-status defaulting to pass), an unreset auto-run guard on the CR-005 empty-output path, an unbounded doctor-run await, a raw-'undefined' error message, and two test-coverage gaps (failure-panel regression detection, untested renderer auto-run wiring); 7 candidates (logger.rs io::Error detail loss, open_log TOCTOU, Windows cmd metacharacters, a failure-panel actions-drop claim disproved by reading the code, an info-only-section drop that is by design, an unreachable ICONS-missing-'info' row status, and a multi-error label-truncation already covered by aggregated remedy hints) were dismissed as unreachable or below the emission floor. No findings were deferred.

standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires '<type>: <short description>'; 8 of 17 subjects use 'EPMCDME-14506 : ...' with no type prefix; later 9 use feat/fix/chore: EPMCDME-14506 style, matching
no code-quality.md guide found at .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md and no ArtifactRef was passed
no security-patterns.md guide found and no ArtifactRef was passed; manually reviewed logger.rs (fixed, non-user log path, no shell interpolation) and health-controller.js; no concrete issue found

findings.title: Commit subjects skip conventional type prefix
findings.problem: 8 of 17 commit subjects in the reviewed range use 'EPMCDME-14506 : <description>' instead of the required '<type>: <short description>' format (e.g. 'EPMCDME-14506 : Track and expose the last health result').
findings.impact: Breaks the documented conventional-commit format the repo's squash-merge workflow relies on for a clean, typed history on main.
findings.recommendation: Reword the offending subjects (or the squash-merge commit body) to lead with a conventional type, e.g. 'feat: track and expose the last health result'.

findings.title: detailFor('AWS CLI') assumes a fixed single item
findings.problem: detailFor unconditionally reads items[0].message to build the AWS CLI row's detail text, assuming the section always has exactly one status line and that it is always first.
findings.impact: A CLI version that adds a second informational line ahead of the version line silently produces the wrong detail text with no bounds or format check.
findings.recommendation: Find the version line explicitly (e.g. by matching a 'Version' prefix) instead of indexing items[0].

findings.title: Info-status agent line renders as a healthy check
findings.problem: agentRow() calls statusOf([item]), which only maps 'error'->'fail' and 'warn'->'warn', defaulting everything else (including an 'info' status line) to 'pass'.
findings.impact: An informational 'Installed Agents' line from the CLI would render as a healthy agent check instead of being excluded or flagged, misrepresenting the section's real status.
findings.recommendation: Have statusOf() (or agentRow) treat 'info' status explicitly rather than falling through to 'pass'.

findings.title: agentRow mis-splits names containing ' - '
findings.problem: agentRow splits an agent's message on the first ' - ' separator to derive title vs. detail (item.message.split(/\s+-\s+/)), assuming that separator never appears inside the name itself.
findings.impact: A future agent/tool name that legitimately contains ' - ' would be mis-split, putting part of the name into the detail field with no guard.
findings.recommendation: Split on a delimiter that cannot appear in an agent name (or use a documented CLI-provided field) instead of the first ' - '.

findings.title: Unrecognized doctor icon silently drops a check
findings.problem: The detail-line regex only matches the five known icons (✓⚠✗○•); a line with any other icon fails to match and its record is dropped entirely rather than surfaced.
findings.impact: A codemie CLI change (new icon, or an icon+variation-selector form) would make an entire check silently vanish from the Health screen with no indication anything was skipped.
findings.recommendation: Fall back to an 'unknown' record (status + raw text) when the icon isn't recognized, instead of dropping the line.

findings.title: Hint-line regex requires exactly six leading spaces
findings.problem: hintMatch requires the following line to start with exactly six spaces (/^\s{6}(.+)$/) to be attached as a hint.
findings.impact: Output whose indentation differs (icon width change, locale-formatted label) causes the hint to be silently treated as a new header/blank instead of attached, with no error raised.
findings.recommendation: Match on leading whitespace generically instead of an exact count, alongside the existing blank-line/header checks.

findings.title: Log-open failure can display literal 'undefined'
findings.problem: handleOpenLog's catch calls showLogError(container, String((e && e.message) || e)); when e is falsy (a rejection with no message and no truthy value), String(e) evaluates to the literal text 'undefined'.
findings.impact: The user sees the word 'undefined' as the failure explanation instead of a useful message.
findings.recommendation: Fall back to a fixed user-facing string when e has no usable message, e.g. e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e ?? 'unknown error').

findings.title: No timeout around the doctor run leaves the screen stuck
findings.problem: run() awaits runStream('codemie doctor', ...) with no timeout; if the underlying process hangs, the await never resolves or rejects.
findings.impact: running stays true forever, so every future recheck, sign-in retry, and the one-shot auto-run become permanent no-ops until the app is restarted.
findings.recommendation: Race runStream against a timeout and treat expiry as a failure through the existing catch/showRunError path.

findings.title: Empty-output failure doesn't reset the auto-run guard
findings.problem: The CR-005-labeled 'zero stdout records' branch shows the run error but never calls onFailure?.(), unlike the catch branch a few lines below which does.
findings.impact: renderer.js's one-shot healthChecked guard is not reset on this failure path, so a user who leaves and re-enters the Health screen after an empty-output failure gets no automatic retry, inconsistent with the catch-branch handling and the onFailure doc comment's stated intent.
findings.recommendation: Call onFailure?.() in the records.length === 0 branch too, matching the catch block's handling.

findings.title: Auto-run-on-first-visit wiring has no test coverage
findings.problem: The healthChecked guard + healthController.run() call inside showView() is exercised by no test in the suite.
findings.impact: Breaking or dropping this block would not fail `npm test` (node --test ui/test/*.test.mjs); health-controller.test.mjs only exercises createHealthController() directly, never through renderer.js's showView().
findings.recommendation: Add a renderer-level test (or extract the guard logic so it's directly testable) asserting run/runStream fires on first navigation to 'health' and not on a second.

findings.title: Failure-panel test stub can't catch a regression to the pre-fix bug
findings.problem: makeEl() gives every stub element a literal _children: [] field; the no-actions test only asserts block.querySelector('.failure-actions') is null, true under both the new `primaryLabel || raw` gate and the old, buggy `actions._children?.length !== 0` gate.
findings.impact: Reverting ui/failure-panel.js's render gate back to the pre-fix check would reintroduce the production bug (an empty, margin-taking actions row always appended) while this test keeps passing.
findings.recommendation: Assert on the actual DOM-visible effect the fix targets, via a stub that only exposes what real Elements expose rather than an internal _children the production check doesn't use.
